items.title: Owning the model matters most for patient data
items.body: The enterprise case for open-weight AI, running it where you control the data, is the version most relevant to the NHS. A model hosted within NHS infrastructure, rather than data passing to a US vendor, is the shape of answer that information governance teams prefer.

items.title: Be cautious about the community pushback on data centres
items.body: A hundred proposed moratoriums and tone-deaf messaging show how local opposition grows. In the UK, the equivalent debate is about energy and water. NHS bodies buying AI should expect questions about it.

items.title: Altman's 'accept some bad things' line
items.body: The fuller argument, that locking AI up has its own risks, is fair, but the NHS context is different: clinical tools have an existing safety framework, and 'some bad things' is not an acceptable standard in a consulting room.
